A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HybridFlow and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Retained experiments and appendix material can be matched despite relocation, rewriting, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark measurements, routing ablations, planner evaluations, and an edge/cloud model-pair swap experiment.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds component ablations, planner validity and fallback measurements, and an offline profiling audit.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix C replace BARTScore-based subtask supervision with marginal end-to-end outcome scores from paired edge/cloud executions, approximated through cached-output recombination. Equation 8 also changes the router input from the subtask embedding alone to the embedding plus cumulative resource consumption. These substantially revise the reported router training and prediction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use GPQA, MMLU-Pro, AIME24, and LiveBench-Reasoning for evaluation, with s1k exemplars and MMLU-Pro/Math500 profiling data. The new diagnostics examine existing coverage. The model-pair swap was already present in v2 Appendix D.2.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds HybridFlow-Chain and HybridFlow-NoCalibration as internal comparison variants. Direct Prompt, CoT, SoT, PASTA, HybridLLM, and DoT remain in the corresponding main comparisons; the relocated model-pair experiment retains its comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix C changes the stated profiling sample count from 3,000 to 2,000. New experiments introduce sequential/no-calibration controls, validity-stratified GPQA evaluation, and profiling-cost measurement. Section 4.1 changes CAPI's description from token counts to API charges, consistent with dollar units already used in v2 tables. Main model configurations, temperature, and budget settings remain; these revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained threshold, planner-SFT, and model-pair analyses, v5 tests removal of DAG parallelism and calibration in Table 3. Appendix C adds planner validity/repair/fallback analysis on GPQA and LiveBench-Reasoning, fallback performance breakdowns on GPQA, and an offline profiling audit in Tables 6–8. These substantially expand mechanism, failure-handling, and overhead analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for main accuracy and latency results. Neither introduces run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new planner validity percentages are descriptive results rather than a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 remain numerically unchanged, including HybridFlow's 55.34% average accuracy and 17.48-second latency. Substantial new diagnostic results appear: Chain and NoCalibration accuracy of 50.62% and 51.85%, planner validity/fallback outcomes, and profiling costs. Threshold prose also corrects the accuracy at threshold 0.6 from approximately 52.61% to 47.85%, matching the already-existing sweep table.

T1.justification: Definition C.2 strengthens valid decomposition requirements from at least one GENERATE sink to exactly one and adds formal dependency consistency using required and produced symbol sets. The knapsack formulation, Lagrangian derivation, and primal–dual discussion otherwise remain substantially unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: Both versions claim dependency-aware DAG execution and learned, budget-adaptive edge/cloud routing improve latency–cost trade-offs while maintaining competitive accuracy on the same four benchmarks. The rewritten abstract and greater emphasis on API costs retain the principal contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly emphasizes fixed-threshold brittleness, whereas v2 emphasized efficient moderate-threshold allocations. Appendix C adds interpretations of fallback latency and affordable one-time profiling. The relocated model-pair discussion strengthens attribution to structural design and drops v2's explicit qualification that broader model-family coverage remains future work. The substantive privacy limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v5 substantially expands implementation disclosure: bounded DAG repair with Rmax=2, edge-confidence rules, chain fallback, outcome verifiers, cached-output recombination, and measured profiling expenditure. The advertised code location also changes from Jiangwen-Dong/Hybridflow-1 to WanyuGroup/ICML2026_HybridFlow. These are meaningful reproducibility and access-information changes, although repository availability was not externally checked.

R1.justification: The BARTScore citation is removed with the changed supervision procedure. The principal related-work coverage and positioning remain. Numerous changed years and venues are publication updates for existing works; the Li/Siyan PAPILLON entries also refer to the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract and related-work discussion are rewritten, and the results and ablation narratives receive substantial revision. Appendix C is expanded and reorganized, and the model-pair discussion moves into the main experiments. The title, affiliations, terminology, and prompt field names are edited, with acknowledgements and an Impact Statement added.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains two rows, three diagnostic tables are added, and v2's appendix model-pair Table 7 becomes main-text Table 4. The notation table, captions, running headers, and prompt presentation are adjusted. Existing plots and diagrams retain their substantive content and basic visual organization.

improvement.justification: The new component ablations and planner validity/fallback audits address previously untested parts of the efficiency argument. Expanded implementation details and corrected threshold prose also improve assessability. The gain is limited by new reporting inconsistencies: Section 4.2 claims a 4–7% accuracy gap although MMLU-Pro accuracy is 72.54% versus CoT's 72.00%, and the NoCalibration utility is not reconciled with its reported accuracy, cost, and benefit–cost definition. The main benchmark results remain unchanged.
